clue.text: Terror rising from the grass-roots ?

parts.note: a sudden fear is pictured as springing up out of a grass whose name is the same word

explanation.surface: Fear spreading upward from ordinary people at the political grass roots.
explanation.walkthrough: Panic grass is a real kind of grass (millet belongs to it), so the fear seems to spring up out of the grass roots.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden overwhelming fright is a synonym for terror.

clue.text: Reading-—daily return

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper
to come back is to return

explanation.surface: A commuter's journey home from the town of Reading every day.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading reads as the English town, but it means reading matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap soft-covered book is something to read.

clue.text: Spanish captain's daughter's well-known reply to Edward?

parts.note: no is a reply, a refusal
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A Spanish officer's daughter turning down a suitor called Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish captain's daughter is set up to turn down Edward with 'No, Ted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous or celebrated means widely recognised.

clue.text: Quick with that double helping of lamb

indicators.note: the helping is given twice over

parts.note: a chop is a cut of lamb served as a helping

explanation.surface: Telling a waiter to hurry up with two lamb chops.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurry up is the meaning of this pidgin phrase for speed.

clue.text: Like Elisha's head, a feature of the altar-canopy

parts.note: the prophet Elisha was mocked as a bald head in the Book of Kings
the chin is one of the features of the face

explanation.surface: A biblical prophet's hairless head compared with a decoration over a church altar.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2 Kings 2 children jeer at Elisha, 'Go up, thou bald head'; that gives BALD, then A and CHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldachin is an ornamental canopy set over an altar or throne.

clue.text: John's up to be 'shot at

parts.note: John ... is the figure of England, and the centre of a target is the thing aimed at

explanation.surface: A man named John is about to come under fire.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bull is the cartoon personification of England, and the bull is the centre of a dartboard or target.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of a target, the bullseye, is what is aimed at.

clue.text: For any girl it's awkward, if she's a singer

definitions.text: For any girl it's awkward, if she's a singer

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters are clumsily arranged and need sorting

explanation.surface: A sore throat is a particular trouble for a girl who sings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' tells you to rearrange ANY GIRL ITS; the whole clue also describes the answer, a throat inflammation that is a singer's bane.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the voice box makes singing hard.

clue.text: A Newfoundland nurse's fruit

parts.note: Nana, the nurse in Peter Pan, is a Newfoundland dog

explanation.surface: A big dog's carer with a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: In J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan the Darling children's nursemaid is Nana, a Newfoundland dog; A NANA'S runs together.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineapple is known by this name in French and many other languages.

clue.text: Hamlet's natural shock accompaniment for Keats with the nightingale

definitions.text: Hamlet's natural shock accompaniment for Keats with the nightingale

parts.words: Hamlet's natural shock accompaniment for Keats with the nightingale
parts.note: Hamlet speaks of this with the thousand natural shocks, and Keats's Ode to a Nightingale opens with it

explanation.surface: A medley of literary allusions to Shakespeare and Keats.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet: 'the heart-ache and the thousand natural shocks'; Keats, Ode to a Nightingale: 'My heart aches'.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional anguish or sorrow is the pain felt by both speakers.

clue.text: Asinine council

definitions.meaning: an adjective meaning donkey-like; the answer is a donkey, so the noun stands for it
The nickname of the National Economic Development Council

explanation.surface: A foolish committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey is the British pet name for an ass; and the National Economic Development Council of 1960s Britain bore the same nickname.

clue.text: Literary work that won't bear watching

definitions.text: Literary work that won't bear watching

parts.words: Literary work that won't bear watching
parts.note: plays on the saying that a watched pot never boils, so a work named after a boiling pot cannot be watched

explanation.surface: A piece of writing too dull or shoddy for anyone to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A watched pot never boils', so the pot-boiling book is one that cannot stand being watched; a potboiler is hack work written just to pay the bills.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack book written only to earn money is a piece of literary work.

clue.text: Judgment may be one in Chancery

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, meaning one
a ward in Chancery is a minor placed under the protection of the Court of Chancery

explanation.surface: A ruling handed down by the Chancery court in a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: Chancery is the English court that took charge of orphaned minors, its 'wards in Chancery'; 'may be' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A decision made by an arbitrator or court is a judgment.

clue.text: How to diminish confusion ? Do this to order

definitions.text: How to diminish confusion ? Do this to order

parts.words: How to diminish confusion ? Do this to order
parts.note: the verb means both to make smaller and, in the phrase about order, to bring a muddle into tidy arrangement

explanation.surface: Advice on tidying a mess by imposing order on it.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'reduce to order' is an old idiom for bringing chaos under control, so the same verb both lessens confusion and puts it in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to make smaller, and in 'bring to order' it means to bring into a settled state.

clue.text: Minor railway for the troops

parts.note: an infant is a minor in law

explanation.surface: A small branch line laid on for soldiers to travel by.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers form a body of troops.

clue.text: Pole that put the Earth in orbit

definitions.text: Pole that put the Earth in orbit

parts.words: Pole that put the Earth in orbit
parts.note: a Polish astronomer showed the planet circling the Sun

explanation.surface: A geographic pole setting the globe spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' reads as a geographic pole but means a person from Poland: the astronomer who set the Earth orbiting the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish astronomer proposed a Sun-centred system with the planets circling it.

clue.text: Stars: naturally, demand such huge salaries

definitions.text: Stars: naturally, demand such huge salaries

parts.words: Stars: naturally, demand such huge salaries
parts.note: film stars ask for enormous pay, and anything to do with stars in the sky shares the same adjective

explanation.surface: Celebrities expect, as a matter of course, vast fees.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both 'relating to the stars' (astronomy) and 'enormously large', so stars naturally ask for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An enormous sum is called sky-high, the way distances in astronomy are vast.

clue.text: Of barbers? No, tailors, confound it !

indicators.note: to confound is to mix up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone denying that tailors are meant, and cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confound it' looks like an oath but means scramble NO TAILORS.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to hairdressing and haircutters.

clue.text: Israel's old investment area

definitions.meaning: ..., a port in Israel, was famously besieged (invested) in the Crusades

explanation.surface: An old financial stake in Israel, measured by its land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' here is the military sense, a siege: the Siege of Acre in 1189-91.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city in northern Israel was besieged by crusaders; and the word is also a unit of land measure of 4,840 square yards.

clue.text: Oriental bird, a friend forever

parts.note: E for East, oriental
a tern is a sea bird
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: An eastern seabird and its mate, together always.
explanation.definitionFit: Always and without end mean forever.

clue.text: Heroic work seen otherwise by Unisex types

parts.note: an epic is a heroic poem

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: A heroic tale viewed differently by people of no fixed gender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unisex' looks like a modern word but epicene is an old one for sharing both genders; 'otherwise' scrambles the second piece and 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicene means of neither or both sexes, so these are androgynous people.

clue.text: Friendly race

definitions.meaning: an old sense of ... is a breed or race, as in mankind

explanation.surface: A good-natured contest or people.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means warm and well-meaning; as a noun it means a type or breed, as in humankind.

clue.text: One of two in the world

definitions.text: One of two in the world

parts.words: One of two in the world
parts.note: the globe is split into a northern and a southern half

explanation.surface: Something so rare that only two exist on Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a rarity, but it means one of the two halves of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe is divided into two halves by the equator, each being one of a pair.

clue.text: Like the range of a northern forest

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north or northern
the Forest of Dean is in Gloucestershire

explanation.surface: Describing the extent of a wood in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forest of Dean is an ancient woodland in western England; 'range' is a mountain range, the Andes.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the South American mountain chain.

clue.text: Sounds, like a daybreak deck job. ?

indicators.note: the clue says the answer is pronounced like the words for daybreak

parts.note: a dawning is a daybreak

explanation.surface: A sailor's chore on deck at first light.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'a dawning' and the answer are said the same way; 'deck' is decorate, not a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate, so the job of decking is decorating.

clue.text: Montezuma, say, in the guise of Sherlock Holmes?

definitions.text: Montezuma, say, in the guise of Sherlock Holmes?

parts.words: Montezuma, say, in the guise of Sherlock Holmes?
parts.note: a Mexican emperor's people, read as A to Z plus TEC: a detective from beginning to end

explanation.surface: The Mexican emperor dressed up as the famous fictional detective.
explanation.walkthrough: Montezuma was a Mexican ruler; split the word as A-Z TEC, a 'tec' (detective) from A to Z, every inch like Holmes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mexican empire's ruler belonged to this pre-Columbian people.

clue.text: Movie-producer's'order of battle

definitions.meaning: the word shouted on set to start filming

explanation.surface: A war-film maker drawing up the battle order of his troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The film director's call starts the cameras rolling; and armed combat is called seeing military engagement.

clue.text: Picture of one of three wise men

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a mage is a magus, one of the three wise men

explanation.surface: A painting of one of the Magi.
explanation.definitionFit: A likeness or representation is a picture.

clue.text: Blows the GI's lights out

definitions.meaning: the bugle call for lights out in the US army

explanation.surface: A soldier's bugler playing the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Light knocks or raps; and the US military bugle call sounded at night.

clue.text: It's nonsense, of course

parts.note: the word means rubbish talk, and is also a dish served as one course of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing an idea as obviously absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as 'naturally', but it points to a course of a meal: tripe is cow's stomach, eaten as food.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish talk is called by the name of the cooked stomach lining served as a dish.

clue.text: The defence one has to copy and pass on ?

definitions.meaning: linked metal rings worn as armour

definitions.text: one has to copy and pass on ?
definitions.meaning: a letter that the receiver must copy and send to others

explanation.surface: A protection you are told to duplicate and forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval armour of interlinked rings; and a chain letter that each receiver must send on to others.

clue.text: For empire-builders the stop is out-of-the-way

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation stop
taken as written

indicators.note: out of order here turns the abbreviation backwards

parts.note: ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: For imperialists, halting is unthinkable.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests stopping is unthinkable; in fact 'the stop' is a punctuation mark and 'out-of-the' turns the street abbreviation round.
explanation.definitionFit: Settlers who take land abroad extend an empire.

clue.text: Off colour, .with potential growing pains ?

definitions.meaning: full of seeds, which may grow

explanation.surface: Feeling a bit poorly, perhaps from growing pains.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ill or unwell; and full of pips that could sprout into plants.
